findings.title: Redirect chain passes through unencrypted HTTP
findings.explanation: When visiting the old domain, the site redirects through an insecure http:// link (http://new-domain.example.com) before reaching the final https:// destination. This middle step is not encrypted, so data in that hop could be intercepted or tampered with, and it also undermines the trust chain for visitors and search engines.
findings.recommendation: Update the redirect on old-domain.example.com to point directly to the https:// version of new-domain.example.com, removing the intermediate http:// hop.

findings.title: Old domain requires three redirect hops to reach final page
findings.explanation: Visitors and search engines going to old-domain.example.com are bounced through three separate redirects before landing on the final page. Each hop adds delay and makes the site slower to load, and can also dilute SEO value being passed to the new domain.
findings.recommendation: Configure a single direct redirect from old-domain.example.com straight to the final https://new-domain.example.com/home URL.

findings.title: No SPF or DMARC records configured
findings.explanation: The domain has no SPF or DMARC records set up. Without these, it's easier for scammers to send fake emails that appear to come from this domain, which can be used for phishing against your customers or partners.
findings.recommendation: Add SPF and DMARC TXT records to the domain's DNS settings, even if the domain only forwards and doesn't send mail directly.

findings.title: TLS certificate valid for 60 more days
findings.explanation: The site's SSL certificate is currently valid and has 60 days left before it expires. This is not urgent yet, but is worth tracking so the site doesn't unexpectedly lose its secure connection.
findings.recommendation: Confirm automatic certificate renewal is set up, or calendar a manual renewal well before the 60-day window closes.
